analysis:
This batch adds CI runner routing: landing.yml (18-28), nightly-linear-package.yml (18-28), provider-release-cache.yml (49-62), plus docs (build.md 151-184, test.md) and a changelog. It touches no provider, coordinator, attestation or crypto code. TB-002, TB-009, TB-011 and the App Attest/serving authorization assets are unaffected. The provider threat model does not cover CI infrastructure, so there are no threat IDs to cite.

Observed controls: each route job has `permissions: {}`, and the caller workflows keep `contents: read`. provider-release-cache.yml routes only pull_request warming to a sandbox, and master/dispatch warming stays on a literal Blacksmith label (line 62). That conditional keeps the release-seeding caches off the sandbox. The docs state that fork PRs and the default-off `DARKBLOOM_ROUTING` variable keep the fallback, that only exact Darkbloom labels are accepted, and that errors fall back. The changelog says release, signing, publication and credentialed jobs stay on Blacksmith.

Unverified (outside the supplied evidence): `.github/workflows/darkbloom-route.yml` and `scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py` are not in this batch. I could not check the label allowlist, fork gating, TLS handling or output sanitization of the plane reply that feeds `runs-on` through `fromJSON`. A compromised or spoofed plane could steer jobs to arbitrary runner labels if that allowlist is weak.

Open question for integration: landing.yml and nightly-linear-package.yml also run on push to master and can route to sandboxes. Their setup-node/setup-python caches could be written at default-branch scope, unlike the provider cache warming that is deliberately kept on Blacksmith. Whether any release or credentialed job restores those cache keys is not shown, so I raise no finding. Other batches (ci.yml, desktop.yml, docs-impact.yml, the route workflow) should be checked for token permissions, secrets exposure on sandbox-routed jobs, and cache scope.
